summary: validate_email is deleted from validators.py and a differently-implemented, weaker validate_email is added to utils.py; this is not a like-for-like move despite the shared name.

items.title: validate_email is deleted from validators.py
items.before: validators.py defined validate_email using an anchored regex (EMAIL_RE) requiring text, an '@', more text, a '.', and more text.
items.statement: validate_email and its EMAIL_RE regex are removed entirely from validators.py; the file no longer performs any email validation.

items.title: A different validate_email is added to utils.py
items.after: utils.py defines a new validate_email that returns True whenever the input string contains an '@' character.
items.statement: A new validate_email function is added to utils.py, but it only checks for the presence of an '@' character rather than the anchored regex the old validators.py function used.

items.title: This is not a like-for-like move
items.before: validators.py's validate_email rejected any string not matching text@text.text exactly.
items.after: utils.py's validate_email accepts any string containing '@' anywhere, including strings like 'a@' or '@@@' that the old function rejected.
items.statement: Despite the same function name reappearing in a different file, this is not a behavior-preserving move: the validation logic materially weakens from an anchored regex match to a simple substring check.
